tickets.title: Transfer stuck "Pending" for 6 hours

customer.name: Ifeoma Chukwu
customer.account_summary: Personal wallet, verified 14 months, average 6 outbound transfers/month, no prior disputes.

messages.text: Good afternoon. I sent NGN 250,000 to my supplier this morning at about 8:40am and it is still showing Pending on my app. My supplier says he has not received anything. He needs this today to release my goods. Please can someone check this urgently?
Please should I just send it again from my other account so he can release the goods, and you refund me later when this one clears?

tickets.hidden_root_cause: The beneficiary bank returned a TIMEOUT response on the NIP (NIBSS Instant Payment) leg during a partner-bank degradation window. Our system correctly queued the transaction for a status requery but a backlog in the requery worker left it displayed as PENDING instead of moving it to REVERSAL_INITIATED. The money never left the customer's wallet-of-record; it is held in a suspense state pending requery, not lost, and not with the supplier's bank.
tickets.red_herring: Customer assumes the money has left the building and reached (or is stuck at) the supplier's bank, and asks to send a second payment 'and get refunded later' — doing this would create a genuine duplicate-payment problem on top of a transient one.

profile.name: Ifeoma Chukwu
profile.notes: No fraud flags. No prior chargebacks.

status_history.note: No further status change recorded; requery worker backlog flagged by monitoring at 12:30.

incidents.description: Elevated timeout rate on inbound credit confirmations for this beneficiary bank during the window. Resolved by partner at 09:20.
Queue depth 340 transactions above normal; on-call paged 12:35.

knowledge_base.title: NIP timeout & requery policy
knowledge_base.body: When NIBSS returns TIMEOUT, the transaction must be requeried within 15 minutes. NIP settles in real time, 24/7, so requery and reversal SLAs run on calendar hours, not banking business hours. If requery confirms the debit did not reach the beneficiary, initiate REVERSAL_INITIATED and credit the customer within 24 hours per CBN guidance on failed electronic transfer reversals. Never advise the customer to resend while a transaction shows PENDING with a TIMEOUT processor_response — this risks a duplicate payment if both eventually settle.

suggested_queries.query: SELECT reference, status, processor_response FROM transactions WHERE reference = 'TRX-9F31A2';
suggested_queries.result_summary: Returns 1 row: status=PENDING, processor_response=TIMEOUT — confirms the NIP leg timed out and was never marked failed or reversed.

suggested_queries.query: SELECT reference, status, processor_response FROM transactions WHERE processor_response = 'TIMEOUT' AND status = 'PENDING';
suggested_queries.result_summary: Confirms this is the pattern to check for stuck-transfer tickets generally: PENDING + TIMEOUT means requery/reversal is owed, not a resend.

root_cause_options.text: Beneficiary bank returned TIMEOUT on the NIP leg; requery backlog kept status at PENDING instead of triggering reversal.
The supplier's bank account is closed or invalid, rejecting the credit silently.
Ifeoma's wallet had insufficient funds and the debit never actually completed.
This is a suspected fraud hold pending manual review.

resolution_options.text: Manually trigger the requery job for TRX-9F31A2, initiate REVERSAL_INITIATED, and credit Ifeoma's wallet within 24 hours if the requery confirms non-delivery; explicitly advise her not to send a second payment.
Tell her to wait 48 hours for the bank to sort it out with no update on system status.
Approve a manual reversal immediately without requerying NIBSS first.
Advise her to send the second payment now since the supplier needs it today.

escalation.target: Payments Ops (requery worker backlog + manual reversal trigger)

tickets.customer_expectation_timeframe: Reversal confirmation within 24 hours (calendar hours — NIP runs 24/7, so this is not tied to banking business hours) if requery shows non-delivery
tickets.model_reply: Hi Ifeoma, thank you for flagging this and for your patience. I've checked TRX-9F31A2 and can see the delay was caused by a timeout between us and your supplier's bank during a short window this morning — your NGN 250,000 has not left your account for good; it's held safely while we confirm delivery. I've triggered a manual recheck with the bank now. If it confirms the transfer did not go through, we will reverse it back to your wallet within 24 hours, and you'll see a status update in your app. Please do not send a second payment in the meantime — if you do and both eventually complete, you'd end up paying twice, and reconciling that takes longer than this fix. I'll follow up here as soon as I have a confirmed outcome, and by end of day at the latest.

tickets.title: Debited twice for one payment at the pharmacy

customer.name: Tunde Balogun
customer.account_summary: Debit card linked to wallet, active 8 months, no prior disputes.

messages.text: I paid NGN 12,500 at MedPlus pharmacy on Allen Avenue this morning with my card linked to your app. I only bought one thing but my transaction history shows two debits of NGN 12,500 each, one after the other. The pharmacy only gave me one receipt. Please refund the extra one, this is not fair.

tickets.hidden_root_cause: The POS terminal timed out waiting for an authorization response after the first swipe. The cashier retried the transaction on the same terminal. Both authorizations actually reached the acquirer and were captured; the acquirer's dedupe logic (which should void a repeated auth within a short window on the same card/terminal/amount) failed to fire, so both were captured as separate, valid debits instead of the first being auto-reversed.
tickets.red_herring: The two transactions have different retrieval reference numbers, which can look like 'two separate legitimate purchases' at a glance — different refs are actually expected for two separate authorizations and does not rule out duplicate-charge; the real tell is same merchant, same amount, seconds apart.

status_history.note: Terminal did not receive auth response within 30s window (auth had actually succeeded upstream at 09:12:09)
Second swipe, same terminal ID TML-7729, same amount
Both auths captured; dedupe rule (same card+terminal+amount within 120s) did not trigger a void on the first.

evidence_required: Two auths, same card, same merchant, same amount, within short window

suggested_queries.query: SELECT reference, retrieval_ref, timestamp, amount_ngn, auth_code FROM transactions WHERE merchant = 'MedPlus Pharmacy - Allen Ave' ORDER BY timestamp;
suggested_queries.result_summary: Returns 2 rows, same merchant/amount, 47 seconds apart, two different auth_codes (A1B2C3, A1B2D7) — two genuine, separately-captured authorizations, not a display glitch.

suggested_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount_ngn) FROM transactions WHERE merchant = 'MedPlus Pharmacy - Allen Ave' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-08-29T09:12:00+01:00' AND '2026-08-29T09:13:00+01:00';
suggested_queries.result_summary: COUNT=2, SUM=25000 — confirms exactly one extra NGN 12,500 capture within a 1-minute window, which is what the chargeback should target.

root_cause_options.text: POS retry after a terminal timeout led to two separate captures because the dedupe/void logic did not fire on the first auth.
The customer actually bought two items and forgot the second purchase.
Card was compromised and used fraudulently at a different location.
The pharmacy manually re-keyed the transaction the next day, causing a second charge.

resolution_options.text: Raise a duplicate-transaction chargeback (reason code 4834) on TRX-A014C9, explain the 5-7 business day refund timeline, no escalation needed.
Refund instantly from the wallet balance without filing a chargeback, absorbing the cost silently.
Tell the customer to dispute directly with the pharmacy since it's their terminal.
Deny the refund because both transactions show status CAPTURED and have different retrieval refs.

tickets.customer_expectation_timeframe: 5-7 business days for the chargeback refund to land

I checked your account and can confirm what happened: the terminal timed out after your first swipe at MedPlus, so it was retried — but both attempts actually went through on our end, which is why you were charged twice for one purchase. I've filed a duplicate-transaction dispute for the second charge of NGN 12,500 (reference TRX-A014C9). You don't need to do anything else on your side; the refund should land back on your card within 5-7 business days. I'll update you here once it's confirmed.

tickets.title: Account locked after "suspicious login"

customer.name: Grace Adebayo
customer.account_summary: Wallet verified 20 months, frequent traveller, previously logged in from 2 countries before.

messages.text: Hi, I can't log in to my account. It says my account is restricted for security reasons. I am currently travelling in London for a work trip and I think I mistyped my login code a few times on a new laptop. Can you please help me get back in? I need to pay for something tonight.

tickets.hidden_root_cause: The risk engine auto-locked the account because three conditions coincided within a 10-minute window: a login attempt from a new, never-seen device fingerprint, a country change (Lagos to London) with no prior travel notice, and three consecutive failed OTP entries. This combination matches the automated account-takeover-prevention rule. All evidence points to this being the genuine customer travelling, not a takeover attempt: her KYC tier is verified, there are no fraud flags, and the failed OTPs match a plausible fat-finger pattern on a new device rather than automated guessing (attempts were 45+ seconds apart, not scripted).
tickets.red_herring: A new device fingerprint AND a new country together look alarming and could be mistaken for account takeover in progress; the real distinguishing signal is the human-paced OTP attempts (not scripted/rapid) plus a clean KYC/fraud history, which together indicate a legitimate traveller, not a takeover.

profile.name: Grace Adebayo
profile.notes: No fraud flags. Prior login history shows occasional travel to Ghana and Kenya, always with prior device registration.

Rule: new_device + geo_change + 3x_otp_fail_within_10min.

Advise the customer to register the new device to avoid repeat locks.

tickets.title: KYC upgrade rejected three times

customer.name: Chidinma Okafor-Nwosu
customer.account_summary: Wallet 5 months old, wants higher transfer limits for a small business.

messages.text: Good morning. I have uploaded my ID three times now to upgrade my account and it keeps saying rejected. I need my limit raised so I can pay my suppliers. My ID is clear, I don't understand why it keeps failing. Please help.

tickets.hidden_root_cause: Chidinma's uploaded ID document shows her legal name as 'Chidinma Okafor-Nwosu' (hyphenated surname, reflecting her married name), while the BVN (Bank Verification Number) record on file shows 'Chidinma Okafor' (unhyphenated, maiden name only). The automated name-matching algorithm scored the match at 78 out of 100, below the 85 auto-approve threshold, causing automatic rejection each time despite the document image itself being clear and genuine.
tickets.red_herring: The customer assumes the document image quality is the problem (since it 'looks clear' to her) and keeps re-uploading the same document, which will never fix a name-matching score issue — the fix is a policy override or supporting document, not a better photo.

field_diff.surname: PARTIAL MATCH (Okafor-Nwosu vs Okafor — subset match, hyphenated addition)

knowledge_base.title: KYC name-mismatch override policy
knowledge_base.body: If the automated name-match score is above 70 and the document authenticity check passes, support/compliance may manually approve with a documented override reason (e.g., 'hyphenated married surname, subset match, DOB confirmed'). If the score is below 70, request a supporting document (marriage certificate or affidavit of name change) instead of overriding.

suggested_queries.query: SELECT submission_attempt, match_score, threshold, outcome FROM customers WHERE customer_name = 'Chidinma Okafor-Nwosu' ORDER BY submission_attempt;
suggested_queries.result_summary: Returns 3 identical rows: match_score=78 every time, always below threshold=85 — confirms re-uploading the same document will never change the outcome; the fix is a policy override or supporting document, not a better photo.

root_cause_options.text: Name-match score (78) falls below the 85 auto-approve threshold due to a hyphenated married surname on the ID vs. maiden name on BVN; document image itself is fine.
The document image is blurry or low quality, causing repeated rejection.
The customer's BVN itself is invalid or does not exist in the national database.
Her account is flagged for suspected identity fraud pending investigation.

resolution_options.text: Since match score (78) is above the 70 floor and document authenticity passed, apply a manual override with a documented reason (hyphenated married surname, DOB match confirmed), and escalate to Compliance for override sign-off.
Ask her to re-upload the same ID document a fourth time.
Reject permanently and tell her Tier 2 is not available to her.
Approve unilaterally without any Compliance involvement since the case seems obviously legitimate.

tickets.customer_expectation_timeframe: Override decision within 1 business day, or a request for a supporting document if declined
tickets.model_reply: Hi Chidinma, thank you for your patience, and I'm sorry for the back-and-forth. I've looked into why your upgrade keeps being rejected: it isn't your document image, which is clear and passes our authenticity check. The issue is that your ID shows 'Okafor-Nwosu' while our records show 'Okafor', so our automated name check can't fully match them on its own. I'm escalating this to our Compliance team with a note explaining the hyphenated married surname and your matching date of birth, so they can manually approve the upgrade. You don't need to re-upload anything for now — I'll follow up within 1 business day with the outcome. tickets.title: Merchant: webhooks not arriving since last night

customer.name: Bayo Ogunleye (Engineering Lead, Kaduna Fresh Foods e-commerce)
rails: Card + bank transfer checkout, webhook-driven order fulfillment
customer.account_summary: Merchant integration live 11 months, ~4,000 orders/month, webhook-dependent order confirmation flow.

messages.text: Since last night our orders are not being marked as paid in our system, but your merchant dashboard shows the payments as succeeded. This is causing real problems — customers are paying but not getting their order confirmations and our warehouse team isn't releasing shipments. Please check urgently, this is a B2B outage for us.
We haven't changed anything on our end recently. Is this an outage on your side?

tickets.hidden_root_cause: The merchant's own infrastructure team rotated their server's TLS certificate at 22:10 the previous night, but the new certificate chain was installed without the required intermediate CA certificate. Our webhook sender performs full chain validation and now receives SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILED on every delivery attempt to the merchant's endpoint. Retries are continuing on the standard 24-hour exponential backoff schedule (window opened 22:14 the previous night and closes 22:14 that night, roughly 13 hours after this ticket was raised), so the merchant has received zero of the 47 queued webhook notifications so far, even though the underlying payments are succeeding correctly on our side. Once the 24h window closes, no further automatic retries will happen — a manual replay after the merchant fixes the cert chain is required regardless.
tickets.red_herring: The merchant states 'we haven't changed anything recently' and asks if it's our outage — this points suspicion at us, but Processor & Partner Status shows all systems green; the actual change (a cert rotation) may not have been visible to the person messaging us if it was done by a different sub-team overnight.

knowledge_base.title: Wrong-network deposits: recovery policy & fee
knowledge_base.body: When a customer sends funds on a different network than the address was issued for (e.g. BEP-20 to an address issued for ERC-20), the deposit is not automatically detected or credited because our listener only watches the expected chain. For EVM-compatible chains (Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum) we control the same address on every chain, so a manual recovery is possible: confirm the tx hash and network on the block explorer, open a wrong-network recovery request with Crypto Ops, apply the standard recovery fee (covers manual sweep and gas), and expect 3-5 business days. Funds sent to a non-EVM chain we do not support (e.g. Tron when we only issued EVM addresses) may not be recoverable; escalate for case-by-case review. There is no instant NGN payout for wrong-network deposits. Educate the customer on selecting the correct network for future deposits. (Simulator content.)

tickets.title: Crypto-to-fiat remittance: received less NGN than quoted

customer.name: Segun Adeleke
customer.account_summary: Wallet 10 months old, occasional crypto-to-NGN remittance, first pricing complaint.

messages.text: Your app quoted me NGN 1,650 per USDT. I sent 300 USDT and expected NGN 495,000, but I only got NGN 486,555. Where is my missing NGN 8,445? This looks like you shortchanged me.

tickets.hidden_root_cause: The quote of NGN 1,650/USDT was locked for 15 minutes from creation (14:02 to 14:17). Segun's exchange withdrawal took 41 minutes to actually settle (a known exchange batching delay outside our control), so his deposit was confirmed at 14:43 — 26 minutes after the quote expired. Per policy, a deposit arriving after quote expiry is converted at the live market rate at time of execution, which had moved to NGN 1,630/USDT (a real, modest ~1.2% rate shift over 41 minutes, not an error). A standard 0.5% off-ramp fee then applies on top, which Segun did not account for in his own mental math. The NGN 8,445 gap reconciles exactly: rate slippage (300 USDT x (1,650 - 1,630) = NGN 6,000) plus the 0.5% off-ramp fee on the executed amount (0.5% x NGN 489,000 = NGN 2,445) = NGN 8,445.
tickets.red_herring: Segun frames this as being 'shortchanged', implying a calculation error or unfair practice; the numbers are fully explained by disclosed, standard policy (quote expiry + off-ramp fee), not an error — the job is to show the math transparently, not to assume fault on either side.

Executed at live rate (1,630) since quote had expired. Gross: NGN 489,000 before fee; 0.5% off-ramp fee (NGN 2,445) then deducted to reach the final payout of NGN 486,555.

knowledge_base.title: Quote locks & rate slippage
knowledge_base.body: Quotes are locked for 15 minutes from creation. If the customer's deposit is not confirmed within that window, the conversion executes at the live market rate at the time of confirmation, not the originally quoted rate. This is disclosed in the quote terms. Exchange withdrawal delays (common due to batching or network congestion) are outside our control but are a frequent cause of missed quote windows. Support should show the customer the exact timestamps and rate history to build trust, and may offer a one-time goodwill fee waiver for a first-time occurrence if policy allows, but should not refund the rate difference itself.

tickets.model_reply: Hi Segun, thanks for flagging this — let me walk you through exactly what happened, because the numbers do add up, just not the way you'd expect. Your quote of NGN 1,650/USDT was created at 14:02 and was only valid for 15 minutes (until 14:17). Your deposit didn't actually confirm on our end until 14:43 — it looks like your exchange's withdrawal took about 41 minutes to settle, which is outside either of our control but did push you past the quote window. Because the quote had expired, your 300 USDT converted at the live market rate at that moment, which had moved to NGN 1,630 — rates do shift even over 20-40 minutes. That rate difference is NGN 6,000 of the gap (300 USDT x NGN 20), with our standard 0.5% off-ramp fee (disclosed at quote time, NGN 2,445 on this amount) making up the rest — together that is your NGN 8,445. So nothing was miscalculated or hidden — the quote simply expired before your funds arrived. Since this is your first time hitting this, I can offer a one-time goodwill waiver of the 0.5% fee (NGN 2,445) for this transaction as a gesture; I don't have the ability to adjust for the rate movement itself since that's a live market rate at the time of execution. For future transfers, sending from a wallet or exchange with faster withdrawal settlement (or choosing a floating-rate order if your platform offers one) will help you lock in quoted rates more reliably.
